Download MeteoGalicia daily observations to station-year files

Source: R/meteogal2download.R
meteogal2download.Rd

Download original daily values and their validation codes in calendar-month windows and save one file per station and year (.rds or .csv). Completed windows are cached, so a repeated call resumes an interrupted download without repeating successful requests. Every file written is recorded in a provenance manifest.

Usage

meteogal2download(
  start_date,
  end_date,
  out_dir = "meteogal_daily",
  station_ids = NULL,
  vars = NULL,
  window_days = NULL,
  format = c("rds", "csv"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

start_date, end_date

Date or "YYYY-MM-DD"; not in the future.

out_dir

Destination folder (relative path recommended).

station_ids

NULL for all stations, or station codes. With explicit IDs, each station is requested separately for safe resumption.

vars

NULL for all variables, or names / native parameter codes requested with idParam (e.g. c("temp_mean", "prec")).

window_days

NULL (calendar months) or a positive integer.

format

"rds" (default) or "csv" (UTF-8, empty string for NA).

overwrite

If TRUE, request the windows again (ignoring the cache) and replace those dates in existing files.

verbose

Show messages.

control

List of max_attempts (3), retry_wait (15 s), sleep_pause (1 s) and timeout (60 s). See meteogal2df().

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame with station_id, year, status (ok, done = everything from cache, nodata, incomplete), n_windows, n_failed, n_files and n_rows.

Details

Files are stored as out_dir/STATION/STATION_YYYY.rds (or .csv). Each contains a base R data.frame with fecha, station metadata, the daily values and one qc_<variable> column per variable with the MeteoGalicia validation code (see meteogal_qc_codes()).

Nothing is filtered at download time: suspect, unvalidated or erroneous values are stored as delivered, with their codes. The quality criterion is chosen later, when reading, with the quality argument of meteogal2df(), meteogal2fdata() or meteogal2lfdata(), so it can be changed without downloading again. No missing value is imputed.

Provenance. out_dir/_meteogal_manifest.csv gets one row per file written: file, station, year, format, rows, first and last date, the requested parameters (idParam), whether validation codes are present, quality_filter = "none (raw values with lnCodigoValidacion)", the download time (UTC), the service URL and the package version. .rds files also carry this information in attr(x, "meteogal_meta") and the units reported by the service in attr(x, "units").

Existing station-year files are merged by station_id and fecha: variables downloaded now replace those dates, other variables and dates are kept. If any window of a station-year fails, its final file is not written (successful windows stay cached); re-run to resume.

Stations are taken from the observations returned in each window, so stations opening or closing during the year are included. No request quota is stated in the service documentation; monthly windows and pauses (control$sleep_pause) keep the load low.

Data source: MeteoGalicia, Xunta de Galicia. Reuse requires citing MeteoGalicia as the source (https://www.meteogalicia.gal/aviso-legal).

References

MeteoGalicia daily JSON service documentation: https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionsDiarios_es.pdf.

See also

meteogal2df(), meteogal2inventory(), meteogal_qc_codes()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
log <- meteogal2download("2024-01-01", "2024-12-31", station_ids = "10157",
                         vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"), format = "csv",
                         out_dir = "meteogal_daily")
log
read.csv(file.path("meteogal_daily", "_meteogal_manifest.csv"))
# Quality is chosen when reading (no new download needed)
x1 <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily", quality = c(1, 5))
x0 <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily", quality = c(0, 1, 5))
} # }
